title: Market Intraday Momentum
one_line: The first half-hour return (from the previous close) predicts the last half-hour return on SPY (R² ≈ 2%, up to 4.8% on high-volatility days); timing the last half hour on that sign earned 6.3%/yr gross vs -0.5% always-in, before costs.

findings.statement: The first half-hour return explains ~2% of the variance of the last half-hour return; adding the 12th half-hour raises R² to ~3.5%, ~4.8% when first half-hour volatility is high.
findings.evidence: SPY from 1999 and QQQ from 1999 to 2012 (working-paper version).

findings.statement: Stronger in recessions and on macro-news days (2006-2009 R² 0.043 / 0.071).
Out-of-sample R² up to 1.8% (first half-hour) and 2.7% (combined).
Holding SPY in the last half hour only when the first half hour was up: 6.3%/yr gross; always holding the last half hour: -0.5%/yr.
Independent replication Aug 2012-May 2014: correlation 0.12, R² 1.4%, driven by extreme first-hour moves.

why.pattern: Late-informed traders and short-gamma hedging push the close in the direction of the morning move.
why.mechanism: Information digested slowly; forced hedgers trade near the close (see Baltussen et al. 2021).

reported_results.headline: R² ≈ 2% (higher on volatile days); timing strategy 6.3%/yr gross.
reported_results.costs_included: No — costs would 'swamp returns' per the replication.

tradable_edge: Covered by noise_area_last_half_hour_es (baseline B2 = direction of the day's move into 15:30). Costs are the main risk.
angles: Already a baseline in the last-30-minutes sheet
data_fit: ES 1-min (ETH + RTH) Dec 2013 → Sep 2026 in clean_ES_master.parquet; NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026. 2024+ is protected in the backtest project.
